description: Skills CRUD - Full CRUD management for reusable agent skills with API, persistence, agent integration, and frontend UI

userStories.title: Create SavedSkill Pydantic data model
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a Pydantic model for skills so they can be validated, serialized, and stored consistently in LangGraph Store.
acceptanceCriteria: Fields: `name` (str), `description` (str, max 1024), `content` (str, SKILL.md body), `tags` (list[str]), `disabled` (bool, default False), `metadata` (dict), `allowed_tools` (list[str]), `license` (Optional[str]), `compatibility` (Optional[str]), `created_at` (datetime), `updated_at` (datetime)
`to_skill_md()` method that reconstructs full SKILL.md content with YAML frontmatter from model fields
Add `SkillCreate` and `SkillUpdate` request schemas, and `SkillListResponse` response schema
userStories.notes: Follow existing pattern in backend/src/schemas/entities/memory.py. Include SkillCreate (name, description, content, tags, allowed_tools, license, compatibility), SkillUpdate (all optional), and SkillListResponse (skills list, total, limit, offset).

userStories.title: Create SkillRepo for LangGraph Store persistence
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a repository layer for skills that follows the existing BaseRepo/MemoryRepo pattern so skill data is persisted in LangGraph Store.
acceptanceCriteria: Constructor: `__init__(self, user_id: str, store: Optional[BaseStore] = None)` calling `super().__init__(user_id=user_id, store=store, entity_type="skills")`
Methods: `create(skill: SavedSkill)`, `get(skill_name: str)`, `update(skill_name: str, ...)`, `delete(skill_name: str)`, `list(limit, offset, query)`
Returns `SavedSkill` instances (no encryption needed, unlike ToolRepo)
userStories.notes: Follow the exact pattern from backend/src/repos/memory_repo.py. Key is skill_name (not UUID). Use _set, _get, _delete, _search helpers from BaseRepo.

userStories.title: Create SkillService business logic layer
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a service layer that wraps the repo and adds business logic like toggle and enabled-skill filtering.
acceptanceCriteria: Constructor: `__init__(self, user_id: str, store: BaseStore)` creating internal `SkillRepo`
`toggle()` returns the updated skill with flipped disabled state
userStories.notes: Follow pattern from backend/src/services/memory.py but use SkillRepo internally. search_enabled filters the result of search() where disabled=False.

userStories.title: Wire SkillService into ServiceContext
userStories.description: As a developer, I need SkillService available through ServiceContext so routes and controllers can access it.
userStories.notes: Two-line change following existing pattern of tool_service, memory_service, etc. in backend/src/contexts/service.py.

userStories.title: Create skill CRUD API routes
userStories.description: As a user, I want REST API endpoints to manage my skills so I can create, read, update, toggle, and delete skills programmatically.
acceptanceCriteria: New file `backend/src/routes/v0/skill.py` with FastAPI router (prefix `/skills`, tags `["Skill"]`)
`POST /skills/search` — List/search skills (query, limit, offset in request body)
`GET /skills/{skill_name}` — Get a single skill by name
All endpoints use `Depends(verify_credentials)` and `Depends(get_store)` with `_get_repo()` helper
Edit `backend/src/routes/v0/__init__.py` to import and register skill router
userStories.notes: Follow the exact pattern from backend/src/routes/v0/memory.py. Use _get_repo() helper, verify_credentials, get_store dependencies. Register in __init__.py like: `from .skill import router as skill` then `app.include_router(skill, prefix=prefix)`.

userStories.title: Integrate skills into agent invocation
userStories.description: As a user, I want my enabled skills to be automatically available to the agent when I chat, so the agent can discover and use relevant skills.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `prepare_skill_files()` function in `backend/src/agents/__init__.py` following `prepare_memory_files()` pattern at lines 73-107
Creates files map: `{"/skills/<name>/SKILL.md": create_file_data(skill.to_skill_md())}` for each enabled skill
Returns `(files_map, ["/skills/"])` when skills exist, or `({}, None)` when no enabled skills

In `backend/src/controllers/llm.py` `llm_invoke()`: call `prepare_skill_files()`, merge skill files as base layer `{**skill_files, **memory_files, **existing_files}`, pass skill sources to `construct_agent(skills=...)`
In `backend/src/utils/stream.py` `stream_generator()`: call `prepare_skill_files()`, merge skill files as base layer before memory files, pass skill sources to `construct_agent(skills=...)`
Agent works normally when no skills are enabled (empty files, None sources)
userStories.notes: The `skills` parameter is already supported by `create_deep_agent()` and threaded through `init_graph()` and `construct_agent()`. Just need to add the prepare function and wire it in the two entry points (llm_invoke and stream_generator). Skill files are the base layer — memory files override, then user files override both: `{**skill_files, **memory_files, **user_files}`.

userStories.title: Write SkillRepo unit tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need unit tests for SkillRepo to verify CRUD operations work correctly with InMemoryStore.
acceptanceCriteria: Test create skill and verify returned SavedSkill has correct fields
Test get skill by name returns correct skill
Test get non-existent skill returns None
Test update skill modifies fields and updates updated_at
Test delete skill removes it from store
Test list skills with search query filter
userStories.notes: Use InMemoryStore from langgraph.store.memory. Follow test patterns from existing repo tests in backend/tests/unit/repos/.

userStories.title: Write SkillService unit tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need unit tests for SkillService to verify service logic, toggle behavior, and search_enabled filtering.
acceptanceCriteria: Test toggle flips disabled field from False to True and back
Test search_enabled returns only skills where disabled=False
Test search returns all skills regardless of disabled state
userStories.notes: Use InMemoryStore. Create SkillService with test user_id. Create mix of enabled/disabled skills to test filtering.

userStories.title: Write prepare_skill_files unit tests
userStories.description: As a developer, I need unit tests for prepare_skill_files to verify file generation, disabled skill exclusion, and SKILL.md format output.
acceptanceCriteria: Test returns ({}, None) when no skills exist
Test returns ({}, None) when all skills are disabled
Test generates correct /skills/<name>/SKILL.md paths for enabled skills
Test SKILL.md content includes YAML frontmatter with skill metadata
Test disabled skills are excluded from output
Test returns correct skill source paths list
userStories.notes: Use InMemoryStore with SkillService to set up test data. Verify the to_skill_md() output format and file map structure.

userStories.title: Create frontend SkillService API client
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I need a TypeScript service class to communicate with the skills API endpoints.
userStories.notes: Follow the pattern from frontend/src/lib/services/memoryService.ts. Use axios with API_URL. search() is POST /skills/search, toggle() is PATCH /skills/{name}/toggle.

userStories.title: Create useSkill hook and SkillContext provider
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I need React state management for skills that fetches from the backend (not localStorage) so skill state is consistent across the app.
userStories.notes: Follow the pattern from frontend/src/context/AgentContext.tsx for SkillContext. Hook should handle loading, error, and refresh states.

userStories.title: Add Skills section to BaseToolMenu (+ button)
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see and toggle my skills directly from the chat input's + button so I can quickly enable/disable skills without leaving the conversation.
acceptanceCriteria: Each skill shown as `DropdownMenuItem` with name + `Switch` toggle
"Manage Skills" link item with `ChevronRight` icon navigating to `/skills`
Active skill count shown as badge on the `+` trigger button
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill
userStories.notes: Import SkillService and useSkillContext. Fetch skills on menu open. Show Switch for each skill inline. Badge count is skills.filter(s => !s.disabled).length.

userStories.title: Create Skills list page
userStories.description: As a user, I want a /skills page that lists all my skills with search, toggle, and action controls so I can manage my skill library.
acceptanceCriteria: Header with "Skills" title, subtitle, and "Create Skill" button
Search/filter text input to filter by name/description, with skill count display
Each skill row shows: name, description (truncated), tag badges, Switch toggle, Edit/Delete action buttons
Toggle calls `SkillService.toggle()` and refreshes list from backend
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill
userStories.notes: Follow the layout pattern from frontend/src/pages/agents/index.tsx. Use ChatLayout wrapper. shadcn Switch, Button, Badge, Input components.

userStories.title: Create Skill create page
userStories.description: As a user, I want an editor page to create new skills with a markdown editor for SKILL.md content and a settings form for metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: Two-tab layout: "Editor" tab (MonacoEditor in markdown mode for SKILL.md content) + "Settings" tab (form fields for name, description, tags, allowed_tools, license, disabled toggle)
Zod validation for form fields, react-hook-form for state management
Submit calls `SkillService.create()` and navigates to `/skills` on success
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill
userStories.notes: Use shadcn Tabs, FormField, Input, Textarea, Switch components. MonacoEditor for markdown. Name field validates kebab-case pattern.

userStories.title: Create Skill edit page
userStories.description: As a user, I want an editor page to edit existing skills, pre-populated with current data, with toggle and delete controls in the header.
acceptanceCriteria: Same two-tab layout as create page: "Editor" + "Settings" tabs
Loads existing skill by `skillName` URL param via `SkillService.get()`
Pre-populates all form fields with existing skill data
Toggle and Delete buttons in page header
Submit calls `SkillService.update()` and shows success feedback
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill
userStories.notes: Use useParams() to get skillName. Reuse similar layout to create page. Delete navigates back to /skills after confirmation.

userStories.title: Add frontend routing and navigation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to navigate to skill pages from the sidebar and via URL so skills are accessible throughout the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit `frontend/src/routes/AppRoutes.tsx` with 3 new routes: `/skills` -> SkillsIndexPage, `/skills/create` -> SkillCreatePage, `/skills/:skillName/edit` -> SkillEditPage (all PrivateRoute)
Edit `frontend/src/components/drawers/app-sidebar.tsx` — Add "Skills" nav link with `Sparkles` icon after Assistants SidebarGroup
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill
userStories.notes: Follow existing route patterns in AppRoutes.tsx. Lazy-load pages. Sidebar link follows existing nav group pattern.

userStories.title: Create wiki documentation for Skills feature
userStories.description: As a user or developer, I want documentation explaining what skills are, how to use the API, and how to manage skills in the UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Sections: What are Skills, API curl examples for all CRUD operations (search, create, get, update, toggle, delete), Using Skills with Agents, UI Guide, Best Practices
Wiki builds successfully (`cd wiki && npm run build`)
